beats.why: The viewer assumes Ellie was arguing with her mother rather than her brother because only Ellie is shown.
The viewer misinterprets two minutes later as Laurel failing to run after her daughter after a fight rather than the timing of Ellie departure.
The viewer assumes Laurel hates her husband for not driving Ellie to school rather than irrationally resenting him simply for being sick.
The guess frames the bodily overdrive as a fight-or-flight response rather than an immune system reaction.
The guess views the two buckets as two separate disasters rather than a psychological substitution of one for the other.
The viewer assumes Laurel is fixating on the morning Ellie disappeared rather than the details of Hannah flat.
Showing Laurel holding the phone leads the viewer to believe a ringing phone triggered her panic.
The viewer assumes the panic is about Ellie rather than Hannah.
Showing only Laurel leads the viewer to believe Laurel is presenting a fake self rather than Floyd.
The worried expression leads the viewer to focus on an anxious state rather than her sloppiness.
The on-screen words lead the viewer to believe criminal methods were learned from library books rather than an abductee leaving only with her books.
The theatre mask icon leads the viewer to suspect active deception of others rather than charming people rationalizing away tragedies to protect their own comfort.
The walking pose and afraid expression lead the viewer to believe he fled after discovering a grave rather than burying the body himself.
The on-screen words lead the viewer to believe an external burglar is being discussed rather than Laurel imagining her daughter as the thief.
The crossed-out words suggest that closure being a myth is rejected, contradicting the narrator's point that closure is indeed a myth.
The on-screen words cause the viewer to interpret the metaphorical void filled with concrete as a literal grave filled with concrete.
The on-screen words highlight bones in the woods without indicating the narrator's comparative point that this is not the hardest part.
Staging mother and daughter together causes the viewer to believe they are collaborating on a shared survival story rather than hearing how the mother's survival story ignored her daughter.
